title: Force a must-do project, with a recorded reason

blocks.text: Problem statement
The planners sent the third request:

**Request 3.** Some projects have to be done whatever the model thinks they are worth: a regulator's order, storm damage, a safety finding. Give us a must-do switch. And every must-do needs a written reason, or the auditors will ask us who forced what, and why.

The change is proposed and archived in `openspec/`, and the living capital-plan spec states its requirements. The specs, the tests (one per scenario, named after it) and the expected report are given and read-only. One scenario of the change has no test yet; it is not part of this step.

You start from the planner with the regional share, where `Request.must_do` is a stub field and `report.overrides` a stub. Make every must-do project start in some year of its window, chosen by the model, without touching its value. Refuse, before solving, an override for a project not in the portfolio, or with no reason. List each override with its reason in the report.

Run executes `main.py`, which plans a tiny portfolio: 12 projects of GridCap, a fictional utility, drawn by `capplan/portfolio.py` from seed 58, over three years with $1,500k a year, a 25% share for Plains and one must-do project, and prints the plan, its overrides, each year's line and the line about the specs; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Blueprint
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
`build` in `capplan/model.py`
def build(projects: list[Project], request: Request) -> Built

items: **Contract.** As before, except that a project in request.must_do gets a row `must_<pid>`, its starts over its window summing to exactly 1, in place of `once_<pid>`.
**Modeling idea.** A must-do is a rule about the plan, so it is a row; the model still chooses the year.

**Taught in** [14.4.3 A Must-Do Override That Needs a Recorded Reason](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/58-project-sdd-openspec/units/unit-03/14.4.3-a-must-do-override-that-needs-a-recorded-reason.unit.html).

blocks.text: `check` in `capplan/request.py`
def check(projects: list[Project], request: Request) -> None

items: **Contract.** As before, and raises ValueError for a must-do override that names a project not in the portfolio, or whose reason is empty or only white space.
**Modeling idea.** The reason is data the model never reads, so it is checked before solving.

**Taught in** [14.4.3 A Must-Do Override That Needs a Recorded Reason](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/58-project-sdd-openspec/units/unit-03/14.4.3-a-must-do-override-that-needs-a-recorded-reason.unit.html).

blocks.text: `overrides` in `capplan/report.py`
def overrides(request: Request) -> list[str]

items: **Contract.** Each must-do override as '<pid>: <reason>', the reason stripped, sorted by project id.
**Modeling idea.** The report says who was forced, and why, next to the plan.

**Taught in** [14.4.3 A Must-Do Override That Needs a Recorded Reason](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/58-project-sdd-openspec/units/unit-03/14.4.3-a-must-do-override-that-needs-a-recorded-reason.unit.html).

blocks.text: `main` in `main.py`
def main() -> None

items: **Contract.** As before, with REQUEST marking P010 must-do with the reason 'Storm damage on the Ridge line, inspection report IR-31', and a line '  must-do <override>' for each override, after the plan's summary line.
**Modeling idea.** The report lists the overrides with the plan.

**Taught in** [14.4.3 A Must-Do Override That Needs a Recorded Reason](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/58-project-sdd-openspec/units/unit-03/14.4.3-a-must-do-override-that-needs-a-recorded-reason.unit.html).

"""GridCap's capital projects: one record per project, and a seeded generator.

GridCap is the course's fictional utility. Every portfolio here is drawn by `generate` from a seed,
and no number in it is a real utility's.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from dataclasses import dataclass

REGIONS = ("north", "plains", "coast")
FIRST_YEAR = 2027


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    region: str
    cost: int        # $k, paid in the year the project starts
    value: int       # $k, what the project is worth to GridCap
    earliest: int    # the first year it may start
    latest: int      # the last year it may start


def generate(n: int, seed: int = 58, years: int = 5) -> list[Project]:
    """n invented projects. Plains projects are worth less per $k, as the planners say they are."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    projects = []
    for k in range(n):
        region = REGIONS[rng.randrange(len(REGIONS))]
        cost = rng.randrange(100, 900, 10)
        ratio = rng.uniform(0.6, 1.5) if region == "plains" else rng.uniform(0.9, 2.4)
        earliest = FIRST_YEAR + rng.randrange(years)
        latest = min(FIRST_YEAR + years - 1, earliest + rng.randrange(3))
        projects.append(Project(f"P{k + 1:03d}", region, cost, round(cost * ratio), earliest, latest))
    return projects

"""Run: a three-year capital plan with a Plains share and a must-do, and a strict check of the specs.

The portfolio is GridCap's and invented: 12 projects drawn by capplan/portfolio.py from seed 58. The
request is scaled down to its size, so the solve is quick. Nothing is read from the working
directory, so the report is the same wherever Run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from capplan.plan import plan
from capplan.portfolio import generate
from capplan.report import overrides, share_by_year, spend_by_year
from capplan.request import Request
from specs_check import passes, requirements, sections, validate

PROJECTS, SEED = 12, 58
REQUEST = Request(budget=1_500, years=3, shares={"plains": 25},
                  must_do={"P010": "Storm damage on the Ridge line, inspection report IR-31"})


def main() -> None:
    projects = generate(PROJECTS, seed=SEED, years=REQUEST.years)
    print(f"portfolio: {PROJECTS} fictional projects, seed {SEED}; budget ${REQUEST.budget:,}k a year")
    got = plan(projects, REQUEST)
    print(f"{len(got.starts)} projects started, value ${got.value:,}k ({got.status})")
    for line in overrides(REQUEST):
        print(f"  must-do {line}")
    plains = share_by_year(projects, got.starts, "plains")
    for year, spend in spend_by_year(projects, got.starts).items():
        starts = sorted(pid for pid, y in got.starts.items() if y == year)
        print(f"  {year}: {len(starts)} starts, ${spend:,}k, plains {plains[year]:.0f}%  {' '.join(starts)}")
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    specs = sorted((root / "openspec" / "specs").glob("*/spec.md"))
    reqs = [r for spec in specs for r in requirements(dict(sections(spec.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))["Requirements"])]
    verdict = "passed" if all(passes(issues) for issues in validate(root).values()) else "FAILED"
    print(f"openspec: {len(specs)} specs, {len(reqs)} requirements, "
          f"{sum(len(r.scenarios) for r in reqs)} scenarios; strict validation {verdict}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
